parts.label: a
parts.ask: The value \(V\) pounds of a mobile phone, \(t\) months after it was bought, is modelled by \(V = ab^t\). A graph of \(\log_{10} V\) against \(t\) is a straight line through \((0, 3)\) and \((10, 2.79)\). Using these points, find the initial value of the phone.

steps.why: Initial means \(t = 0\): read the intercept, then undo \(\log_{10}\).

parts.answerText: The initial value of the phone is £1000.

parts.label: b
parts.ask: Find a complete equation for \(V\) in terms of \(t\), giving the exact value of \(a\) and the value of \(b\) to 3 significant figures.

steps.why: Take logs of \(V = ab^t\): intercept \(\log_{10} a\), gradient \(\log_{10} b\).

parts.label: c
parts.ask: Exactly 2 years after it was bought, the phone was worth £320. Use this to evaluate the reliability of the model.
parts.method: Compare the model's value with the real one
parts.answerText: The model predicts £314.94, which is close to the actual £320 (under 2% out), so the model is reliable.
